title: EU retail volume softened in July as non-food demand fell while food sales rose
source_unit: Eurostat Euro indicators, Volume of retail trade, July 2026
geography: European Union and euro area; seasonally adjusted retail-trade volume and calendar-adjusted annual comparisons by sector and Member State

observations.period: July 2026 compared with June 2026; seasonally adjusted retail-trade volume

denominator.unit: EU and euro-area retail trade volume indices, base year 2021, by retail sector

euro_area_total_monthly.unit: percent change in total retail-trade volume from June 2026

eu_total_monthly.unit: percent change in total retail-trade volume from June 2026

euro_area_food_monthly.unit: percent change in food, drinks, and tobacco retail volume

euro_area_nonfood_monthly.unit: percent change in non-food retail volume excluding automotive fuel

euro_area_fuel_monthly.unit: percent change in automotive-fuel retail volume

eu_food_monthly.unit: percent change in food, drinks, and tobacco retail volume

eu_nonfood_monthly.unit: percent change in non-food retail volume excluding automotive fuel

eu_fuel_monthly.unit: percent change in automotive-fuel retail volume

mechanism.value: The July demand pattern is category-selective: food volume grew while non-food and fuel volume declined, consistent with households protecting essential consumption while delaying or reducing more discretionary purchases

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Eurostat first estimates using seasonally adjusted retail-trade volume indices; categories exclude automotive fuel where specified.
observations.uncertainty: The release is an aggregate monthly index and does not identify households, prices, product quantities, cultural goods, income, debt, or causal effects of confidence or inflation; first estimates can be revised.
observations.subgroup: EU and euro-area retail sectors: total, food/drinks/tobacco, non-food excluding automotive fuel, and automotive fuel.
observations.counterinterpretation: Category movements may reflect tourism, weather, promotions, supply, fuel prices, calendar effects, or substitution across channels rather than household financial stress; food volume growth does not prove unchanged food affordability.

observations.period: July 2026 compared with July 2025; calendar-adjusted annual retail-trade volume

denominator.unit: EU and euro-area retail trade volume indices, with Member State comparisons where data are available

euro_area_total_annual.unit: percent change in total retail-trade volume from July 2025

eu_total_annual.unit: percent change in total retail-trade volume from July 2025

euro_area_food_annual.unit: percent change in food, drinks, and tobacco retail volume

euro_area_nonfood_annual.unit: percent change in non-food retail volume excluding automotive fuel

euro_area_fuel_annual.unit: percent change in automotive-fuel retail volume

eu_food_annual.unit: percent change in food, drinks, and tobacco retail volume

eu_nonfood_annual.unit: percent change in non-food retail volume excluding automotive fuel

eu_fuel_annual.unit: percent change in automotive-fuel retail volume

largest_country_increases.value: Cyprus +8.6%, Latvia +7.1%, and Sweden +6.4% in total retail volume

largest_country_decreases.value: Romania -5.7%, Germany -2.5%, Italy -1.0%, and Spain -0.7% in total retail volume

mechanism.value: A positive annual aggregate masks a wide country and category dispersion: essential volume is stronger than fuel and non-food, while national consumer demand diverges sharply

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Eurostat annual retail-volume comparisons; Member State rankings apply only to countries with available data and use calendar-adjusted indices.
observations.uncertainty: Annual volume indices do not measure household welfare, affordability, retail margins, cultural spending, or within-country inequality; country composition and revision status require caution.
observations.subgroup: EU, euro-area, and Member State retail-trade aggregates by sector.
observations.counterinterpretation: Country variation can arise from tourism, exchange rates, weather, fuel-price exposure, population, promotions, and statistical coverage rather than distinct consumer cultures or confidence effects.

boundary: This record adds observed EU retail-volume behavior to the confidence and household-expectations layers. It does not establish household-level substitution, discretionary cultural spending, affordability, causal sentiment effects, or durable consumer welfare.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Eurostat July 2026 Euro-indicator release reviewed for monthly and annual EU/euro-area total, food, non-food, fuel, and Member State retail-volume comparisons, index adjustments, first-estimate status, and sector definitions.
